improv_extras.concept: build a form by CSG boolean ops on SDF primitives (smooth-min union/subtraction) and clothe the resulting surface in particles — a carved, solid object

v1.feedback: Strong SDF boolean interpretation — the smooth-union/subtraction CSG skull is technically honest and the rejection-sampled surface reads as bone within two seconds. Palette (bone/ash/deep-brown) is exemplary. For refinement: the breathing amplitude (0.045) is so subtle it may be invisible at default camera distance — consider doubling it to 0.09 or adding a second slower frequency to the cranium particles so the skull feels alive, not static. The dust motes at opacity 0.1 are nearly invisible; raising to 0.16–0.18 would give the atmosphere more archaeological haze without competing with the form.

v2.feedback: The SDF boolean skull is a strong literal execution of the prompt — CSG union/subtraction of cranium, jaw, orbits, nasal cavity is real boolean sculpture, and the Plensa reference lands. The chain requirement ('continuous morph from parent ecn / deus-ex-machina') is the weak link: the piece reads as a standalone bone reliquary, not as ecn transformed by the word — consider adding a morph state or residual geometry from the parent so the lineage is visible, not just captioned. The breathing amplitudes and 28k particle density are well-calibrated; the 800 dust motes add atmosphere without becoming noise. Palette is excellent — bone-on-dark-earth with warm key and cool fill is exactly the archaeological register this form wants.
